alleppey-backwaters.summary: Alappuzha (Alleppey) is the gateway to Kerala's backwaters: a network of lagoons, canals and lakes lined with coconut palms. November to February is dry and cool, and houseboat season is in full swing.

reach.rail: No railway. Ships also run from Chennai, Kolkata and Visakhapatnam, but take days.
reach.road: Roads on each island connect main sights. Ferries link the islands.

andaman-islands.summary: The Andamans are one of India's best islands for diving, snorkelling and beaches. The dry season runs from about November to April, with calm seas and the easiest ferries.

ayodhya.best: October to March. Ram Navami (March-April) and Deepotsav (Oct-Nov) are very crowded.

coorg.summary: Coorg is a hilly district in the Western Ghats, known for coffee estates, waterfalls, Kodava culture and cool weather. Winter is dry, green and fragrant with coffee harvest.

darjeeling.summary: Darjeeling offers sunrise over Kanchenjunga from Tiger Hill, the UNESCO-listed toy train, world-famous tea gardens and Buddhist monasteries.

dwarka.summary: Dwarka, the western dham, is home to the Dwarkadhish temple, the Nageshwar Jyotirlinga nearby and Bet Dwarka island, now reached by the Sudarshan Setu bridge.

goa.summary: Goa is India's favourite beach state, with Portuguese-era churches, spice farms, quiet Hindu temples like Mangueshi and Shantadurga, and a relaxed coastal lifestyle.

Never step off the boat in tiger zones.
sundarbans.etiquette: Keep noise and litter down. Respect restricted areas and the rules of the forest department.
sundarbans.best: November to February is dry and comfortable. Avoid the monsoon and cyclone season (June-September).

reach.air: Kolkata (CCU) is the nearest airport.
reach.rail: Canning or Sonakhali stations connect to Kolkata's suburban network.
reach.road: About 100 km from Kolkata to Godkhali, 3-4 hours.

sundarbans.summary: The Sundarbans is the world's largest mangrove forest, a UNESCO site shared with Bangladesh, where rivers meet the Bay of Bengal. Boat safaris go through winding creeks in search of tigers, crocodiles and birds.

sites.x: The hill temple of Venkateswara, among the most visited in the world.
sites.tip: Book a timed darshan slot on the TTD site before you travel. Plan the whole day. Phones may not be allowed.

sites.x: A temple of Padmavathi, about 5 km from Tirupati. Many pilgrims visit this too.
An old temple in the centre of Tirupati.
A Shiva temple with a waterfall at the foot of the hills.
A natural rock arch near Tirumala.
A waterfall spring on the hill.

tips: Book darshan and rooms on the official TTD website only - it opens bookings months ahead.
Traditional dress is required for darshan (dhoti/kurta-pyjama for men; saree/salwar with dupatta for women).
Mobile phones and cameras are not allowed inside; use the free deposit counters.
tirupati.etiquette: Strict dress code and no photography inside. Respect queue rules; touts selling 'quick darshan' are illegal.
tirupati.best: September to February is most comfortable. Brahmotsavam (Sept/Oct) and Vaikunta Ekadasi are spectacular but extremely crowded.

reach.air: Tirupati Airport (TIR) at Renigunta, about 15 km from Tirupati, has flights from Hyderabad, Bengaluru, Delhi, Mumbai and other cities. Chennai airport is about 140 km away.
reach.rail: Tirupati (TPTY) and Renigunta (RU) stations are connected to Chennai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Mumbai, Kolkata and Delhi.
reach.road: Frequent APSRTC buses link Tirupati with Chennai (about 140 km), Bengaluru (about 250 km) and Hyderabad. TTD free buses and APSRTC buses run up the ghat road to Tirumala.

tirupati.summary: The Sri Venkateswara temple at Tirumala is among the most visited shrines in the world, famous for its darshan system, hair-offering tradition and laddu prasadam.

sites.x: Go near sunset for views of the City Palace and island palaces.
Allow two hours for courtyards, painted rooms and the crystal gallery.
Walk the lanes around Jagdish Temple and Gangaur Ghat for miniature paintings and spices.
The hilltop palace has a wide view over the lakes.

sites.n: Day trip to Kumbhalgarh and Ranakpur
sites.x: Combine the fort wall and the Jain temple in one long day.

tips: Book lake-view hotels early for December.
Many palace areas charge separate entry fees.
Beware of touts selling boat rides; use official ticket counters.
udaipur.etiquette: Dress modestly in temples and cover your shoulders in the palace temples.
udaipur.best: October to March. December and January are cool and busy; summer is hot.

reach.air: Maharana Pratap Airport (UDR) at Dabok is about 22 km from the city, with flights from Delhi, Mumbai, Jaipur and Ahmedabad.
reach.rail: Udaipur City station has trains from Delhi, Jaipur and Ahmedabad.
reach.road: About 400 km from Jaipur and 260 km from Ahmedabad. Buses and taxis are frequent.

udaipur.summary: Udaipur is Rajasthan's most romantic city, with white palaces reflected in Lake Pichola, narrow bazaars, craft markets and hill forts nearby. Winter, from November to March, is the best time.

sites.x: The pre-dawn aarti for which Ujjain is best known. Reporting is very early.
sites.tip: Advance booking is needed on the temple's official website. Strict dress code. Carry the ID used to book.

sites.x: The south-facing Jyotirlinga of Shiva, one of the twelve.
sites.tip: Queues vary a lot. Ask about the paid quick-darshan option on the official site. Phones and bags are usually not allowed inside, so use the cloakroom.

sites.x: A walkway of large sculptures and murals telling Shiva stories, next to the temple.
sites.tip: Best in the evening when it is lit. Good for photos and a slow walk.

sites.x: A Shakti temple. Tradition counts it among the Shakti Peethas. Known for its tall lamp towers.
sites.tip: Visit at dusk, when the lamps are lit.

sites.n: Ram Ghat and the Shipra aarti
sites.x: The main bathing ghat on the Shipra, with an evening aarti.
sites.tip: Check the evening aarti time locally. Be careful on wet steps.

sites.x: A temple of Kal Bhairav, the guardian of the city in tradition. Liquor is offered as prasad here.
sites.tip: Local shops outside sell the offering. Queues build up in the late morning.

sites.x: Tradition says Krishna, Balarama and Sudama studied here under Guru Sandipani.
sites.tip: Quiet and short. Combine with Mangalnath.

sites.x: Tradition names this the birthplace of Mars (Mangal). Popular for Mangal dosh pujas.
sites.tip: Pujas are priced by the priests, so agree the amount first.

sites.x: A large Ganesh image close to Mahakal.
sites.tip: Easy stop on foot before or after Mahakal.

sites.x: An old Ganesh temple across the Shipra.
sites.tip: Pair with Kaliadeh Palace.

sites.x: A Kali temple linked in popular tradition with the poet Kalidasa.
Caves linked to the king-turned-ascetic Bhartrihari, on the Shipra bank.
sites.tip: Low roof inside. Mind your head.

sites.x: An 18th century astronomical observatory, built on the Karka Rekha idea.
sites.tip: Ticketed. Check opening hours.

sites.x: A palace on an island in the Shipra, a short drive from the city.
sites.tip: Best in the late afternoon light.

sites.x: Ujjain's classic morning meal, sold near the main temple area.
sites.tip: Eat where locals queue. Choose freshly made items.

tips: Book Bhasma Aarti as early as possible - it fills up.
Stay in Ujjain the night before the aarti.
Indore is a great base for food lovers.
ujjain.etiquette: Strict dress code for the garbhagriha and Bhasma Aarti.
ujjain.best: October to March. Shravan Mondays and Mahashivratri are very crowded.

reach.air: Devi Ahilyabai Holkar Airport, Indore (IDR), about 55 km away.
reach.rail: Ujjain Junction (UJN) is connected to Delhi, Mumbai, Ahmedabad, Kolkata and other cities.
reach.road: About 55 km from Indore and 190 km from Bhopal; frequent buses.

ujjain.summary: Ujjain is home to the south-facing Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga, its unique dawn Bhasma Aarti and the Mahakal Lok corridor, and hosts the Simhastha Kumbh on the Shipra.

sites.n: Registration and yatra slip at Katra
sites.x: Registration is needed before you begin the trek.
sites.tip: Register online beforehand where possible.

sites.x: A walk of about 12 to 13 km. Ponies, palanquins and helicopters are available.
sites.tip: Start early. Carry water and rain gear.

sites.x: The shrine of Vaishno Devi in a cave temple.
sites.tip: Queues move in batches. Bags and phones are not allowed inside.

sites.x: A halfway point with a small cave temple.
A temple above the Bhawan, visited after the darshan by tradition.
sites.tip: Extra 1.5 km climb, or use the ropeway.

sites.x: A cave shrine of Shiva, about 80 km from Katra.
sites.tip: Check road and cave access first.

tips: Carry your yatra registration card - it is checked at Banganga.
Night trekking is common and the path is lit; carry a light jacket.
Leather items and bags are restricted inside the cave; use the lockers.
vaishno-devi.etiquette: Maintain queue discipline at the Bhawan. Do not litter on the trek route.
vaishno-devi.best: March to June and September to October. Navratri is auspicious but crowded. Winter (Dec-Jan) brings snow and cold; monsoon can cause slippery paths.

reach.air: Jammu Airport (IXJ) is about 50 km from Katra, with flights from Delhi, Mumbai, Srinagar and others. Taxis and buses run to Katra.
reach.rail: Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Katra (SVDK) station has direct trains, including Vande Bharat, from New Delhi and other cities.
reach.road: Katra is about 50 km from Jammu by road. J&K SRTC and private buses run frequently.

vaishno-devi.summary: The holy cave of Mata Vaishno Devi on the Trikuta mountains is reached by a well-paved trek of about 12-13 km from Katra, with ponies, battery cars and helicopters for help.

sites.n: Sunrise boat ride on the Ganga
sites.x: A rowing boat along the ghats at dawn, from Assi to Dashashwamedh.
sites.tip: Agree the fare and time before boarding. Wear something warm in winter.

sites.x: The main Shiva temple of Kashi, reached by the redeveloped Vishwanath corridor.
sites.tip: Phones and bags usually go in lockers. Check the temple's official site for slots and queues.

sites.x: A temple of Annapurna, the goddess of food, near Vishwanath.
sites.tip: Short stop on foot.

sites.x: Tradition names Kaal Bhairav as the guardian of Kashi.
sites.tip: Many pilgrims visit him after Vishwanath.

sites.n: Walk the ghats and Manikarnika view
sites.x: A slow walk along the ghats. Manikarnika is the main cremation ghat.
sites.tip: Do not photograph the cremations. Keep respectful distance and ignore touts offering guided views.

sites.x: A well-loved Hanuman temple. Tuesday and Saturday are the busiest days.
sites.tip: Phones usually not allowed inside.

sites.x: The Buddhist site where the Buddha gave his first sermon, about 10 km out.
sites.tip: The museum has a weekly closing day. Check before going.

sites.x: The evening aarti on the river. Many sit on boats or on the steps.
sites.tip: Arrive 45 minutes early for a good spot. Watch your belongings.

sites.x: A large marble temple inside the Banaras Hindu University campus.
sites.tip: Check the campus entry rules for visitors.

sites.n: Banarasi food trail: kachori, tamatar chaat, lassi
sites.x: Kachori-sabzi and jalebi for breakfast, tamatar chaat and malaiyo in season.
sites.tip: Choose busy stalls. Drink only bottled water.

tips: Book stays near Assi, Dashashwamedh or Godowlia to stay walkable to the ghats.
Photography of cremations at Manikarnika is considered disrespectful - do not do it.
Use only the official temple website for darshan bookings; ignore touts offering 'VIP' entry.
varanasi.etiquette: Dress modestly for temples. Remove footwear before entering ghats-side shrines. Ask before photographing sadhus or rituals.
varanasi.best: October to March is pleasant. Summers (April-June) are very hot; during monsoon the river rises and some ghats and boat services close.

reach.air: Lal Bahadur Shastri International Airport (VNS) at Babatpur, about 25 km from the city centre, has direct flights from Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Bengaluru, Hyderabad and other cities. Prepaid taxis and app cabs are available.
reach.rail: Varanasi Junction (BSB) and Banaras (BSBS) stations are well connected to all major cities, including Vande Bharat services from Delhi. Pt. Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Junction (DDU), about 17 km away, handles many long-distance trains.
reach.road: Varanasi is on NH-19. State and private buses run from Prayagraj (about 120 km), Lucknow (about 300 km) and Gaya (about 250 km).

varanasi.summary: One of the oldest living cities on earth, Varanasi is home to the Kashi Vishwanath Jyotirlinga, the evening Ganga Aarti and more than eighty ghats along the holy river.
